QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_44

question.text: Under Section 5.14, the Social Impact Assessment Report should be:

answer.text: Delivered orally to save time and paper
In writing, containing a clear expression of the SIA's findings — the SIA should NOT report orally
Delivered only to SEBI, not the SE or intended users
Standardised to a single fixed format across all SAS standards, with no tailoring permitted

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.14 is explicit: 'The social impact assessment report should be in writing and should contain a clear expression of the social impact assessor's findings. Oral and other forms of expressing conclusions can be misunderstood without the support of a written report. For this reason, the social impact assessor should not report orally.' The Trap: A directly contradicts Section 5.14. C mis-identifies recipients — the report goes to engaging party and intended users. D is wrong — the framework explicitly permits tailoring to area-specific circumstances. Cross-Exam Context: NISM III-A / III-C compliance-report frameworks also demand written reports; XXIII extends it with comprehensive/convincing/balanced tests. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Attach a one-page executive summary in plain English to every AIR — stakeholders (esp. beneficiaries and donors) rarely read past page 1, so the written-summary is where your findings actually land.
